satow-tasj-vol7:
Volume Seven of the Transactions, from 1879, gathers the years 1878 to 1879. Satow's Ancient Japanese Rituals gives this volume its lasting fame. His texts rank as the first English versions of the norito prayers.

Other papers treat history, folklore, language, and nature in the usual mix. The pioneer scholars report from a Meiji Japan changing month by month. Each yearly volume works as a time capsule of early discovery there. The norito texts alone earn the book a place in Shinto studies. Readers meet Japan's oldest prayers in English for the first time in print. Satow's renderings opened a door that later scholars walked through for decades.
coke-reports-1777-vol7:
The seventh volume of Wilson's 1777 edition closes Coke's Reports. The full set records the decisions of England's greatest judge across the turning of the seventeenth century. When Wilson finished the edition, the Reports had already served the bar for well over a hundred years.

The final volume completes the case law with the last of Coke's reported decisions and the indexes that make the set usable. Taken together, the Reports founded the common law's case method: the idea that law grows from decided disputes, carefully kept. Lawyers on both sides of the Atlantic trained on Coke, and the American founders cited him as an authority on liberty. The edition Wilson made remained the one lawyers used for a century, and it still anchors any serious shelf of English legal history.
